introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, graph paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source. Les faits cités (régions, institutions, sites) sont ceux de la géographie du Cameroun couramment enseignée ; les chiffres sont arrondis et donnés avec « about » quand ils ne sont pas certains ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. À relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Les faits cités sont à vérifier avant mise en avant : noms d'institutions et de sites (par exemple Wakwa, Jakiri, Waza, Korup, Campo-Ma'an, Dja, Lobeke, SODECOTON, CICAM), séries chronologiques (insécurité du Nord depuis environ 2013-2014, abattage d'éléphants vers 2012) et ordres de grandeur ; tout chiffre précis a été omis ou donné avec « about ».

questions.enonce_markdown: 4. a) Describe any TWO major relief regions of Cameroon in terms of: the average height, two main landforms and orientation of the land. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Two relief regions are required (4 marks each: average height 1, two landforms 2, orientation 1).**

**1. The Western (Bamenda-Bamileke) Highlands.**

- *Average height*: mostly between about 1,000 and 2,000 m, with peaks higher (Mount Oku at about 3,000 m and the Bambouto Mountains at about 2,700 m).
- *Main landforms*: volcanic mountains and massifs with craters and crater lakes (for example the Oku and Bambouto massifs and Lake Nyos); basalt plateaux and high plains (the Bamenda and Bamileke plateaux and the Ndop plain), cut by steep escarpments and deep river valleys (for example the Ring Road area).
- *Orientation*: the highlands form a chain trending from the south-west to the north-east (the Cameroon Volcanic Line, from Mount Cameroon on the coast to the Adamawa), and they separate the coastal lowland from the Benue and Chad basins.

**2. The Adamawa Plateau.**

- *Average height*: about 1,000 to 1,200 m (commonly given as about 1,100 m above sea level), the highest point being the Tchabal Mbabo massif.
- *Main landforms*: a broad undulating basalt and granite plateau with grassy plains; residual hills and inselbergs, volcanic cones and block-faulted scarps (the Tchabal massifs, the Ngaoundere escarpment); waterfalls on the rivers at the plateau edge (for example the Vina falls) and wide flat-bottomed valleys.
- *Orientation*: a plateau trending roughly south-west to north-east, in the centre of the country, dividing the forested south from the savanna north.

*(Other acceptable regions: the Coastal Lowlands, the South Cameroon Plateau, the Northern Lowlands (Benue and Chad basins) and the Mandara Mountains.)*

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Explain how market and transport means have influenced the main system of agriculture in the Coastal Lowlands. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**The main system is large-scale commercial plantation agriculture (banana, oil palm, rubber, tea and cocoa/coffee on smaller holdings), together with food-crop farming for the towns.**

**Influence of the market (4 marks).**

- The big **external market** (Europe and the world market for banana, palm oil, rubber) and the **large local market** of Douala, Limbe, Kumba, Edea and other towns encouraged large estates producing for sale (cash crops) rather than subsistence crops.
- Industrial and urban demand led to **processing factories** (palm oil mills, rubber factories, banana packing stations) inside or near the plantations, which ensured buyers for all the output.
- Near the towns, a ring of small farms grows **perishable food crops** (plantain, cassava, vegetables, fruits) for the town markets, because there is a ready market.

**Influence of the transport means (4 marks).**

- The coast has **seaports** (Douala, Limbe, Tiko, Kribi) which make exports cheap; the plantations are close to them (bananas need quick shipping: they were grown close to ports and railheads).
- Roads (Douala-Edea, Limbe-Kumba, plantation feeder roads) and the Douala-Yaounde and Douala-Kumba railways carry produce to the ports and bring labour, fertilisers and machinery.
- Good transport lets perishable crops such as bananas and vegetables reach the market fresh in refrigerated lorries and ships; where roads are poor, farmers grow less perishable crops.
- The transport network also draws migrant labour from the hinterland to the plantations.

*Marks: market 4; transport 4 (explanation, not listing).*

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Briefly examine any THREE efforts by the government of Cameroon to improve on livestock production. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Any three efforts (about 2 to 3 marks each, 7 in all).**

1. **Research and improved breeds.** Government stations and research institutes (for example IRAD and the Wakwa station in Adamawa, and the Jakiri livestock station in the North-West) carry out breed improvement, cross-breeding and artificial insemination, and supply improved bulls, pigs and chicks to farmers.
2. **Animal health and veterinary services.** The Ministry of Livestock, Fisheries and Animal Industries runs vaccination campaigns against the main cattle diseases, dips, veterinary posts and tsetse control, which reduce losses of animals.
3. **Pasture and water development.** Boreholes and dams, the improvement of pastures, the organisation of transhumance and the creation of grazing zones, and conflict management between farmers and herders.
4. **Marketing and processing.** Cattle markets, abattoirs and cold-storage facilities (for example at the main cattle-collecting centres), roads and the railway to Ngaoundere to supply the southern towns.
5. **Training, credit and support.** Extension agents train farmers, and credit, subsidies and support programmes help common initiative groups and young farmers to start poultry, pig and cattle projects.

*Marks: three efforts named and briefly explained.*
